req.title: DELETE rejects unknown player
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 on DELETE for a non-existent playerId.

doc.reasoning: The DELETE endpoint is at /players/squadnumber/{squad_number}. R-PLAYER-015 requires HTTP 404 when the squad_number does not exist. Tests cover: (1) positive case — a squad_number that exists in the pre-loaded DB returns 204 (proving the route works and the 404 is conditional, not universal); (2) negative case — a squad_number that does not exist returns exactly 404; (3) boundary case — squad_number 0 (below the minimum seeded value of 1) returns 404; (4) boundary case — squad_number 27 (one above the maximum seeded value of 26) returns 404; (5) decision-table case — squad_number 26 (last seeded row, exists) returns 204, confirming the boundary between existing and non-existing. These tests together kill mutations that flip the 404 constant, invert the existence check, or change the comparison operator in retrieve_by_squad_number_async.

tests.name: test_delete_existing_player_returns_204
trace: R-PLAYER-015: confirms the 404 is conditional on non-existence, not always returned

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from main import app

client = TestClient(app)

def test_delete_existing_player_returns_204():
    r = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/10')
    assert r.status_code == 204
    assert r.content == b''

test_delete_existing_player_returns_204()

tests.name: test_delete_nonexistent_player_returns_404
expected: Status code is exactly 404, not 200, 204, or 400
trace: R-PLAYER-015: primary error pathway — unknown playerId must yield 404
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from main import app

client = TestClient(app)

def test_delete_nonexistent_player_returns_404():
    r = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/9999')
    assert r.status_code == 404
    assert r.status_code != 204
    assert r.status_code != 200

test_delete_nonexistent_player_returns_404()
